directAnswer: Yes, WiFi can function without an internet connection, allowing devices to communicate with each other over a local network.
summary: WiFi creates a local network that enables device-to-device communication, independent of internet access.

sections.heading: Using WiFi for Local Networking
sections.body: Devices connected to the same WiFi network can share files, stream media, and play games together without needing an internet connection.

sections.heading: Common Applications Without Internet
sections.body: Applications like file sharing, local gaming, and media streaming can operate effectively on a WiFi network without internet access.

steps.title: Connect Devices to WiFi
steps.detail: Ensure all devices you want to connect are connected to the same WiFi network. This can usually be done through the WiFi settings on each device.

steps.title: Set Up File Sharing
steps.detail: On devices like Windows, enable file sharing in the Network and Sharing Center. On macOS, use the Sharing preferences to share files.

steps.title: Use Local Apps
steps.detail: Open applications that support local networking, such as multiplayer games or media servers, and ensure they are set to use the local network.

faqs.question: Can I print over WiFi without internet?
faqs.answer: Yes, if your printer is connected to the same WiFi network, you can print documents without needing internet access.

faqs.question: Will my smart home devices work without internet?
faqs.answer: Some smart home devices may work locally, but many require internet access for full functionality and remote control.

faqs.question: How can I access shared files without internet?
faqs.answer: As long as your devices are on the same WiFi network, you can access shared files through file sharing settings on each device.

caveats: Certain features of devices may be limited without internet access, such as software updates and cloud services.
